title.rendered: UST Pre-med Student Internship With SHIP and the SAIL Clinics

content.rendered:
From classroom learning to community-based practice.

From July to August 2026, pre-med students from the University of Santo Tomas, College of Science, Department of Biological Sciences joined SHIP Academy for a Clinical and Research Internship across our #SAILClinics.

Throughout their rotation, the students gained first-hand exposure to clinical and public health practice while taking part in hands-on research, from understanding patient care pathways to working with health data and contributing to research activities.

We’re glad to have shared our work and our commitment to evidence-based, person-centered care with the next generation of health and science professionals.

Thank you from the crew at SHIP!

title.rendered: #AIDS2026 Poster Presentation: “Disengagement From and Re-engagement in HIV Care”

content.rendered:
“People don’t move through HIV care in a straight line—and our health systems shouldn’t assume they do.”

SHIP is excited to share our latest research presented at the now concluded #AIDS2026, examining how clients transition through HIV care across our four community-led SAIL Clinics. Using multistate survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards models, we found that delayed ART initiation, educational attainment, employment, and viral hepatitis significantly influence both disengagement from and re-engagement in HIV care.

These findings reinforce the need for person-centered, differentiated service delivery that supports clients throughout their care journey, not just at the point of treatment initiation.

Better HIV outcomes require more than getting people into care. Better HIV outcomes require helping people stay connected to care.

title.rendered: #AIDS2026 Poster Presentation: Predictors of Choice Between HIV Self-Testing With or Without PrEP

content.rendered:
HIV self-testing is opening doors to #PrEP—but not equally for everyone.

Data from SAIL TelePrEP (January to September 2025, n=4,955) shows that HIV self-testing is a powerful gateway into PrEP: 2 in 3 clients who came in for self-testing chose to combine it with PrEP on the spot.

Who was most likely to say yes to PrEP?

Clients aged 45 years and older (4.7x more likely)

Employed and student clients

Those reporting condomless sex or shared needle use—meaning risk-informed decision support is working

But geography still matters. The SAIL Clinics operate in Metro Manila and Region 4-A. Clients residing outside these areas had significantly lower odds of choosing PrEP, even after accounting for demographics and risk, serving as a reminder that digital health still runs into very physical barriers.

The takeaway: HIV self-testing accessed via remote platforms like TelePrEP and other telehealth options are meeting people where they are—we now need regional PrEP hubs to meet them where they live.

title.rendered: #AIDS2026 Poster Presentation: HIV Testing Outcomes by Geographical Mobility and Testing History

content.rendered:
At the #AIDS2026 poster exhibition, SHIP’s Dr. Patrick Eustaquio presented our study exploring how geographical mobility influences HIV testing outcomes among men who have sex with men and among transgender women accessing HIV services.

The analysis included more than 15,500 clients from the SAIL Clinics, a network of community-based clinics strategically located near major transport hubs in the Greater Metro Manila area. By operating where people travel, work, and connect, these clinics are uniquely positioned to serve highly mobile communities.

Dr. Eustaquio conveyed the study’s findings, which showed that people being screened for HIV for the first time were more likely to have a reactive HIV screening result than repeat testers, particularly among the clinics’ local residents and transient clients. These results truly highlight the importance of designing HIV services that reflect how people live and move, and how they access care.

title.rendered: “Loved by users, limited by systems: Qualitative insights into LAI-PrEP” Oral Abstract Session at #AIDS2026

content.rendered:
At #AIDS2026‘s oral abstract session entitled “Loved by users, limited by systems: Qualitative insights into LAI-PrEP [Long-Acting Injectable Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis],” our SHIPmate, Dr. Rod Olete moderated the discussion in the panel, who all came from communities working to make long-acting prevention a reality everywhere.

Insights were brought by the experts, tackling the issues of convenience and discretion versus efficacy, injection discomfort, and even the adoption of LAI-PrEP in communities affected by conflict and displacement. The panel highly agreed that the real barriers for these HIV prevention options are structural—the concerns being cost, insurance, mobility, and stigma, and not personal reluctance.

As the Philippines prepares for the national rollout of the LAI-PrEP medication, lenacapavir, this year, the lesson from the session and the International AIDS Conference becomes clear: Access has to be built with the same intention as the science. Choice only means something if the system delivers it.

title.rendered: SHIP receives Grindr for Equality’s Community Innovation Award at #AIDS2026

content.rendered:
Sustained Health Initiatives of the Philippines (SHIP) was selected as a recipient of the inaugural Community Innovation Award by Grindr for Equality, presented during #AIDS2026 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil! Mohan Sundararaj, Managing Director of Grindr for Equality, and Jen Hecht, Cofounder & Director of Building Healthy Online Communities (BHOC), presented the award to SHIP’s Medical Director, Dr. Kate Leyritana, together with the Director for Clinical Programs, Dr. Patrick Eustaquio, and Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, Research, and Learning Specialist, Dr. Rod Olete.

The Grindr for Equality Awards celebrate individuals’ and organizations’ valuable work in shaping our HIV response, giving special recognition to “exceptional leadership advancing HIV prevention, LGBTQ+ health equity, and access to care worldwide.”

With the honor of the Community Innovation Award and the support of Grindr for Equality, SHIP is bolstered even more to continue bridging HIV self-testing, PrEP, and mental health support to those who need it most, and strengthened to further serve as a model in its innovative and community-centered approaches to HIV prevention and healthcare.

“When the roadmap meets reality.” 🦜

At #AIDS2026 in Rio de Janeiro, SHIP’s Rod Olete presented at the conference’s Satellite session of “Barriers and Facilitators of Person-Centred Care for Key and Vulnerable Populations.”

Sharing years of data from the SAIL Clinics and SAIL TelePrEP, Dr. Olete imparted how same-day ART initiation drives better outcomes, especially for the populations who need HIV healthcare the most: transgender and gender-diverse clients, unemployed clients, and clients outside Metro Manila.

He also shared how TelePrEP access grew 435% from 2023 to 2026, and is now formally recognized under the DOH Administrative Order 2026-0005 as a differentiated mode of PrEP service delivery.

With these findings from SHIP’s initiatives and successes, he underlined how person-centered care and community-led care work—peer navigation, telehealth logistics, outreach, and infrastructure—needs real financial investment and domestic support.

With Dr. Olete and the rest of the SHIP crew, we are proud to bring SAIL’s community-led model to the global stage! #TogetherWeSAIL! 🚢⛵

Sustained Health Initiatives of the Philippines (SHIP Inc.) brings the experience of the SAIL Clinics Network, TelePrEP, and our digital mental health & harm reduction initiatives to the global stage— built on a simple belief: the people closest to the epidemic should lead the response.

This week, we join the global community to share what we’ve learned, listen to what others are building, and keep pushing key population-led, digitally-enabled HIV care forward — together. 

Come join us in Rio, in person, or online.

The 26th International AIDS Conference, July 26–31, 2026.

Rethink. Rebuild. Rise.

title.rendered: #AIDS2026: Operationalizing Person-Centred Care in Community-Based Clinics in the Philippines

content.rendered:
A roadmap can tell us where we need to go. But can we actually get there?

The global consensus on person-centred care in the HIV response offers an ambitious roadmap for transforming how HIV services are designed and delivered [https://doi.org/10.1002/jia2.70071]. But translating consensus into routine practice is where the real implementation challenge begins.

At AIDS 2026, we bring this roadmap into the realities of community-based HIV service delivery in the Philippines. Drawing from the experience of the SAIL Clinic network, the presentation explores a practical question: Can the global roadmap for person-centred HIV care be feasibly operationalized within a community-based organization; and what happens when global aspirations meet the realities of everyday service delivery?

The question is no longer simply whether person-centred care is desirable. We already know that it is. The more difficult question is whether it is feasible, implementable, and sustainable within real-world HIV care systems—and what needs to change when it is not.

Because the true test of a roadmap is not whether we agree with the destination, but whether it can help us navigate the realities of getting there.

See you with the International AIDS Society soon at AIDS 2026! aids2026.org

title.rendered: Ahoy, SHIPmates: TelePrEP is SAILing in Cebu!

content.rendered:
TelePrEP padulong na sa Cebu!

SHIP shares gratitude and congratulations to our own SAIL Teleprep Cebu crew for their successful opening and first run, with thanks to the great work of our SHIP and SAIL TelePrEP NCR crew, especially to our Medical Director, Dr. Kate Leyritana.

With SAIL TelePrEP Cebu, HIV self-test kit and #PrEP HIV protection delivery services will be brought easier and quicker to those in Cebu, Central Visayas, and beyond.

Our communities in Cebu, Central Visayas, and nearby areas can find further information and set appointments to start PrEP and get their PrEP refills and HIV self-test kits through linktr.ee/SAILTelePrEP_Cebu. #TogetherWeSAIL!

Across the Philippines, people thrive when HIV services reflect their real lives, not the other way around. Rethinking the response means listening deeply, rebuilding trust through person-centered care, and rising with communities whose insights continue to transform the landscape of prevention and treatment.

At SHIP and our SAIL clinics, we see every day how accessible PrEP, respectful telehealth, and peer-led support open new pathways for choice and dignity. As we move toward AIDS 2026, we join the call to reimagine services that honor autonomy, protect privacy, and make care truly reachable for all.

A future where no one is left behind starts with the voices of people whose lives reflect diverse identities, needs, and aspirations. Rising together means strengthening community-owned spaces where judgment has no place and where people can access HIV services in ways that feel safe, affirming, and empowering.

Through SHIP’s programs—from telehealth-based PrEP navigation to community-rooted mental health support—people are leading the direction of care themselves. Their stories guide how we rebuild systems that uphold dignity, connection, and choice. This is how we rise: side by side, community to community.

To rise as a global community, we must rethink what inclusive, respectful, and human-centered HIV services truly look like. It means rebuilding approaches that recognize pleasure, connection, and safety as essential parts of people’s lives. It means creating systems where privacy is protected, access is convenient, and support is empathetic.

At SHIP, our SAIL clinic network continues to evolve: expanding TelePrEP, widening mental health and harm reduction support, and ensuring care remains welcoming for all key populations. These shifts reflect a simple truth—when care honors people’s lived experiences, everyone is better positioned to thrive.

Join us as we #RethinkRebuildRise with the International AIDS Society this 2026!
